Let

\[
x=\frac{2\sqrt{ab}}3=\frac{2\sqrt q}{3},
\]

and let \(K_\nu\) denote the modified Bessel function of the second kind. The desired pairs are exactly

\[
\boxed{
(a,b)>0,\quad
a+b>3\sqrt{ab}\,\frac{K_0\!\left(\frac{2\sqrt{ab}}3\right)}
{K_1\!\left(\frac{2\sqrt{ab}}3\right)},
\quad
ab\ge \frac{2(a+b+2)^3}{9(2(a+b)+13)}.
}
\]

Equivalently, in the notation \(s=a+b,\ q=ab\),

\[
\boxed{
s>3\sqrt q\,\frac{K_0\!\left(\frac{2\sqrt q}{3}\right)}
{K_1\!\left(\frac{2\sqrt q}{3}\right)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
q\ge \frac{2(s+2)^3}{9(2s+13)}.
}
\]

Here \(0<q\le s^2/4\) is automatic from \(a,b>0\).

**Derivation.**

Write \(z=\rho(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\). In either mode,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log \rho
=
-1+3\sin\theta\cos\theta.
\]

Let \(r=\tan\theta\). Then the projective dynamics are

\[
\dot r=-3r^2\quad\text{in mode }1,
\qquad
\dot r=3\quad\text{in mode }2.
\]

The stationary densities \(p_1,p_2\) on \(r>0\) satisfy zero flux, hence

\[
p_2=r^2p_1,
\]

and solving the stationary equations gives

\[
p_1(r)=C r^{-2}e^{-(br+a/r)/3},
\qquad
p_2(r)=C e^{-(br+a/r)/3}.
\]

Thus the top almost-sure Lyapunov exponent is

\[
\lambda_{\rm as}
=
-1+3\int_0^\infty \frac{r}{1+r^2}(p_1+p_2)\,dr
=
-1+3C\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-(br+a/r)/3}}r\,dr.
\]

Using

\[
\int_0^\infty r^{\nu-1}e^{-\beta r-\gamma/r}\,dr
=
2\left(\frac{\gamma}{\beta}\right)^{\nu/2}
K_\nu(2\sqrt{\beta\gamma}),
\]

normalization gives

\[
C=\frac{\sqrt q}{2sK_1(2\sqrt q/3)},
\]

so

\[
\lambda_{\rm as}
=
-1+
\frac{3\sqrt q}{s}
\frac{K_0(2\sqrt q/3)}{K_1(2\sqrt q/3)}.
\]

Therefore almost-sure exponential stability is exactly

\[
s>3\sqrt q\,\frac{K_0(2\sqrt q/3)}{K_1(2\sqrt q/3)}.
\]

For mean-square stability, track the conditional second moments

\[
(X_i,Y_i,Z_i)=\mathbb E[(x^2,xy,y^2)\mathbf 1_{\sigma=i}].
\]

The resulting \(6\times6\) linear system is positive. Put \(u=\lambda+2\), and define

\[
\Delta=(u+a)(u+b)-ab=u(u+s).
\]

Eliminating the moment variables from the eigenvalue equations gives the Perron eigenvalue condition

\[
\Delta^3-36q\Delta-324q=0.
\]

Mean-square exponential stability fails exactly when the Perron spectral abscissa is nonnegative. At \(\lambda=0\), \(u=2\), so

\[
\Delta_0=2(s+2).
\]

Thus failure of mean-square stability is

\[
\Delta_0^3-36q\Delta_0-324q\le0.
\]

Substituting \(\Delta_0=2(s+2)\),

\[
8(s+2)^3-72q(s+2)-324q\le0,
\]

which simplifies to

\[
q\ge \frac{2(s+2)^3}{9(2s+13)}.
\]

Combining the strict almost-sure condition with the non-strict mean-square failure condition gives the boxed answer.
